  file with the credential, once the camera has connected), and to a phone already paired by a `stream.key` command.
  Only the manager sends `stream.key`: the dashboard's command route refuses it (403), for the administrator too, and
  the command is kept and audited with the id in place of the passphrase. A pairing from a QR code carries none; the
  phone is sent it when it first connects.
- **The phone** (camera app 0.9.63) keeps it, encrypts its stream with it from its next connection on, and says which
  passphrase it holds by that id (`stream_key_id` in its telemetry; the capability is `stream_encryption`).
- **The relay asks for it only once the phone has it.** When a phone's telemetry shows its camera's id, the manager
  puts the passphrase in `<data>/relay/relay.json` (owner only) and the relay makes that camera's listener again with
  it. From then on a caller with no passphrase, or another one, fails SRT's handshake and never connects; what the
  relay passes to OBS over the loopback, and keeps in the spool, is the stream decrypted.

sections.doc: Recordings and the camera relay
sections.title: Each camera's stream is encrypted, and only its own phone can send it
trail: The camera relay: the look-ahead, and each camera's own file
sections.text:
- **Nothing is cut to do it.** A stream that was already arriving goes on as it is, unencrypted, until its next
  connection: the readiness says so, and *Restart SRT* (off air) encrypts it. A phone connects to the manager before
  it streams, so in practice it has its passphrase before its first stream.
- **A phone on an older app keeps working, unencrypted**, and its readiness says so until it is updated.
- **With the relay off** (or unable to run here) OBS listens for the cameras itself, and is given no passphrase: the
  phones are told to drop theirs, so that OBS does not refuse them, and the streams are not encrypted. The readiness
  says so on every camera. (OBS could be given the passphrase in its source's address, but that would put it in
  OBS's scene collection and log, and changing a source's address restarts it; the relay is on by default, and is
  where this is done.)

sections.doc: Recordings and the camera relay
sections.title: Each camera's stream is encrypted, and only its own phone can send it
trail: The camera relay: the look-ahead, and each camera's own file
sections.text:
Each camera's readiness has a **Stream encryption** line: *encrypted*, *will be encrypted* (not streaming, and only a
caller with its passphrase is let in), or why not yet. Removing a camera forgets its passphrase. Tried on this
computer with the camera app's own SRT library (RootEncoder 2.8.1, run on the desktop) against the relay: the right
passphrase connects and its stream arrives whole; none, or a wrong one, is refused. **Tried with one real phone** (a Galaxy
S23, on this code before it was numbered 0.9.63): the hand-over to an unarmed phone, an encrypted 4K stream at 25 Mbit/s
through the relay, *Restart SRT*, a Wi-Fi drop, a new passphrase while on air (the stream ran on, and its next connection
used the new one), the passphrase kept across the phone's restarts and taken away again under a relay from before this,
and callers with none and with a wrong one refused. Not tried: several phones at once, or a whole show.

sections.doc: Recordings and the camera relay
sections.title: Each camera's own file of a recording
trail: The camera relay: the look-ahead, and each camera's own file
sections.text:
For a videographer who wants to cut the show themselves, every programme recording can come with each camera's own
file and the director's cuts as an edit of them. Switch it on as administrator, **Keep each camera's own file of every
programme recording** under Recordings › PC recordings (not while the programme is being recorded). Then, beside a
programme recording `<name>.mkv`:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `<name> cameras/01 Pixel 8.mp4`, … | each camera's stream, from a few seconds before the recording to a few after, as it was streamed: not re-encoded |
| `<name>.edl` | the programme as a CMX 3600 edit of those files: open it in Resolve, Premiere or Final Cut Pro with the folder beside it |
| `<name>.cameras.json` | where each camera file starts against the programme, its length, and anything that could not be made |

They are made in the background once the recording stops, in about the time it takes to copy the streams; the
dashboard's programme panel says when they are ready. The directed programme itself is ready at once, as before.

sections.doc: Recordings and the camera relay
sections.title: Each camera's own file of a recording
trail: The camera relay: the look-ahead, and each camera's own file
sections.text:
- **The edit allows for the delay.** The programme shows each camera its delay after it reached this computer; camera files
  are placed by both, and each recording notes the delays as it starts.
- **Lined up to the frame.** Each camera file is placed against the programme from when its pictures reached this
  PC, taken over the whole file so that a burst cannot throw it out. Tested to within one frame at 30 fps.
- **Disk.** With camera files on, the spool keeps about ten minutes (`relay_keep_minutes`) while nothing is recorded,
  and everything from the start of a recording until its files are made, so at the end of a show each camera is on
  disk twice. A 4K camera set to 25 Mb/s kept about 30 Mb/s, some 13 GB an hour (six of them, with the spool on the
  programme's disk, about 160 GB an hour). The readiness check's disk estimate counts each camera, only with camera
  files on, at the rate the relay measures, else the rate it is set to stream at, else `camera_mbps` (32); the
  programme at the rate of the last recording, else `program_gb_per_hour` (6). A spool on a disk of its own is checked
  on its own.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Architecture and commissioning status
sections.text:
Android still uses the existing independent H.264 recording encoder, AAC and
MediaStore MP4 output in **Movies / Concert Camera**. SRT and pinned WSS control
are unchanged. A separate single-thread worker uploads only registered,
successfully finalized MP4s. SQLite maps immutable recording IDs to app-created
MediaStore URIs; no command accepts a filesystem path or shell deletion command.
WRITING, UNCERTAIN and DELETED entries are never upload candidates. A process
crash leaves WRITING entries excluded rather than assuming finalization.

This registry begins with files created by 0.6.0 and later. Older phone files are preserved
but are not automatically adopted: earlier versions did not persist reliable
finalization/ownership records. Session ID is reported as null unless capture's
`session_id` was assigned; production-session coordination is not implemented.
No session identity is fabricated. Scans page in batches of 100 and report
individual unreadable/invalid files independently.

Manager upload/verification and recovery tests pass on disposable fixtures;
Android 0.6.1 was installed with approval. Actual pinned-HTTPS offload, pause,
resume after manager and Android process restarts, independent hash/FFprobe
verification, and retained-source rescan passed on Pixel 3; cleanup remains disabled. **Actual cleanup is disabled by default and has not been
performed on real recordings.** Do not enable it until on-device fixture tests
also pass. Existing SRT/camera operation has not been interrupted by development.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Workflow
sections.text:
1. Open `/offload` on the same authenticated localhost dashboard (normally
   `http://127.0.0.1:8088/offload`). Existing dashboard password and CSRF protection
   apply. The page supports the configured camera capacity, including more than 5, with a card for each paired
   camera showing only the buttons that apply to it. The steps below are the page's four numbered steps (1. Window,
   2. Copy, 3. Check, 4. Clean up); the one to do now is marked **Now**, and each notice at the top of the page
   carries the button it names, asking the same questions as the step's own button.
2. Stop production recording in OBS and stop camera streaming/local capture during
   offload. Choose a window length (10 minutes to 12 hours), click **Open offload window
   (OBS idle)** and confirm. The window expires automatically and is closed after a manager restart. Until OBS
   state monitoring is implemented, this explicit operator interlock is required;
   the manager cannot detect an OBS recording started outside it. Close the window
   or pause transfers before starting OBS again.
3. **Scan All Cameras** (or Scan camera). Offline requests stay queued. Hashing is
   on a background thread and pauses if capture resumes. Results include ID,
   stable device ID, session ID, filename, creation time, duration, bytes and SHA-256.
4. Select recordings and choose **Offload Selected**, or **Offload All Completed**.
   Jobs are version-bound and deduplicated in SQLite. One device uploads at a time
   by default. Pause/resume/cancel/retry operate on the durable queue; cancellation
   retains partials and originals. Retry starts the failed transfer from byte zero
   and preserves any failed final destination in quarantine.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Workflow
sections.text:
5. Files stay `.partial` until exact length, independent destination SHA-256 and
   FFprobe media validation pass. FFprobe scans packets, requires a readable video
   track and duration matching the source within max(2 seconds, 2%). This is media
   container validation, not a full decode or guarantee of recording quality.
6. Atomic rename produces `<job-id>.mp4`, with original filename/session metadata
   kept in SQLite. Directory and file fsync precede durable verification. Sources
   stay intact. **Verify Files** rechecks destination files independently.
7. When commissioning has passed and cleanup is explicitly enabled, select verified
   recordings, **Approve Cleanup**, then **Clean Verified Originals**. These are two
   separate confirmations. A second verified backup is strongly recommended; this
   version does not create or enforce one automatically. There is no automatic
   retention policy. Offline cleanup remains REQUESTED, never falsely successful.
8. The agent checks its owned URI, finalized state, ID, exact bytes and a fresh full
   SHA-256 before `ContentResolver.delete`. Journalled approval IDs make retries
   idempotent, including a process exit after deletion but before acknowledgement.
   The manager re-verifies destination and current source inventory before sending
   cleanup and records each device's final acknowledgement/free space/error.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Configuration
sections.text:
Add these optional keys to the manager's private `data/config.json`, then restart
its user service. No root or cloud service is needed.

```json
{
  "recording_library": "/home/you/Downloads/ConcertCameraManager/data/recordings",
  "ffprobe_path": "/home/you/Downloads/ConcertCameraManager/tools/ffmpeg-package/extracted/usr/bin/ffprobe",
  "camera_network_cidr": "192.168.100.0/24",
  "offload_concurrency": 1,
  "offload_reserve_bytes": 1073741824,
  "offload_defer_streaming": true,
  "obs_recording_active": false,
  "offload_cleanup_enabled": false
}
```

`obs_recording_active: true` is an additional manual hard interlock; false does not
open an offload window. Concurrency is clamped to 1–8 devices; a lease expires after
30 seconds without progress so an unavailable device cannot hold the queue forever.
Stale/missing telemetry blocks transfers. Android also defers while SRT is requested,
connecting, connected, stopping or reconnecting, and while local recording is active.
Android currently permits only a literal manager IPv4 address on 192.168.100.0/24
and binds upload sockets to that Wi-Fi network, excluding cellular/Ethernet/VPN
fallback and redirects. Other network plans require extending this validation first.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Configuration
sections.text:
Chunks carry explicit server offset and recording-version headers. The manager
states the chunk size in each work reply (4 MiB by default, `offload_chunk_bytes`,
at most 8 MiB). App 0.7.0 sends chunks back-to-back in 15-second slices and
re-reads the queue between slices, so pause/cancel still take effect; app 0.6.1
keeps sending one 1 MiB chunk per two-second poll (~0.5 MiB/s). Every chunk is
still synced to disk before its offset is committed.

Verified files are published as `<camera name>/<recording date>/<original
name>-<job id prefix>.mp4` with a `.json` sidecar (camera, original filename,
session, size, SHA-256), so the library stays identifiable without the database.
Files verified before this layout remain at `<job id>.mp4`.

Phone cleanup is switched with `python -m camera_manager --data-dir <dir> cleanup
enable|disable` followed by a manager restart.
SQLite and partial files persist across app/manager restarts. The manager's committed
offset is authoritative after a lost reply; uncommitted partial tails are truncated.
Hashing restarts after interruption, while upload resumes from the saved offset.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Configuration
sections.text:
No secrets are hardcoded. Uploads use HTTPS on the existing TLS agent listener,
the per-device Bearer credential and certificate pin **plus hostname verification**.
The server checks approved client subnet, ownership, body and request-rate limits.
Dashboard mutations require login, CSRF token and permitted origin. Filenames are
metadata only; server paths use generated UUIDs. Protect the recording library and
SQLite backups with ordinary filesystem permissions. The audit table records scan,
queue, pause/resume/retry, verification, approval, cleanup delivery and final results.

FFprobe was absent on the workstation. Official Ubuntu `ffmpeg` package
`7:6.1.1-3ubuntu5` was downloaded and extracted to project-local tools; **no system
packages or OBS settings changed**. The existing host FFmpeg shared libraries load
it successfully. Set `ffprobe_path` as above or use a separately installed FFprobe.
A missing executable fails verification and prevents cleanup.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview
sections.title: Build and tests
sections.text:
```bash
cd /home/you/Downloads
ConcertCamera/tools/build-debug.sh --offline
ConcertCameraManager/.venv/bin/python -m pytest ConcertCameraManager/tests -q
```

APK: `ConcertCamera/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` (0.6.1 preview).
Install only after approval, in place with the compatible debug key, never clear
app data or remove recordings. Restart manager only outside active production;
pairing credentials and its SQLite registry are preserved.

The tests (`tests/test_offload.py`) use temporary
libraries, fake device credentials and disposable fixture bytes/MP4 copies.
They cover success, interruption/resume, manager restart, simulated agent-process
restart, offset/version/ownership conflicts, hashes, truncation, disk-full/write
failure, pause/cancel/concurrency, duplicate requests, changed source inventory,
destination tampering, approval/ack rejection and unavailable cleanup recipients.
Real TLS/HTTPS upload and real FFprobe fixture verification run too. Browser checks
cover login, five cards, inventory, queue/pause/resume/scan and disabled cleanup.
Actual Android process restart/resume was tested. MediaStore deletion and five
physical devices remain untested;
no real source recording is deleted by the tests.

Supported storage APIs and media-validation references:
- https://developer.android.com/training/data-storage/shared/media
- https://ffmpeg.org/ffprobe.html

sections.title: Files changed
sections.text:
Android:
- `RecordingInventory.kt`: durable app-created URI registry, finalized-only scan,
  duration/SHA-256, individual scan errors, transfer ledger and guarded deletion.
- `RecordingOffload.kt`: independent pinned HTTPS worker, approved Wi-Fi binding,
  progress, chunk offsets, deferral, retries and cleanup acknowledgements.
- `RecordingOutput.kt`, `CaptureService.kt`: register new files and mark only clean
  finalization eligible; retain failed/uncertain recordings.
- `ControlAgentService.kt`: start/stop the worker with the authenticated control
  agent and report offload status in telemetry.
- Manifest: normal ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE permission for approved-network checks.
- Gradle/MainActivity: preview version 0.6.1; existing toolchain and media retained.

sections.doc: Verified recording offload — 0.6.1 preview

sections.text:
Linux:
- `camera_manager/offload.py`: SQLite jobs/inventory/audit, durable partial writes,
  leases/concurrency, independent hash/FFprobe verification, atomic publication,
  manual cleanup approval and acknowledgement checks.
- `camera_manager/routes/agents.py` (the phones' side) and `camera_manager/routes/offload.py` (the dashboard's): authenticated device HTTPS and dashboard/CSRF APIs,
  network/size/rate limits, deferred scheduling and explicit idle window.

The actual transferred 128,160,204-byte / 50.806-second Pixel fixture also fully
video/audio decoded using the existing standalone verifier: 1,516 H.264 1080p
frames at approximately 20 Mbps, 2,376 AAC frames, monotonic timestamps and no
B-frames. Both phone test originals remain intact. Final manager service was
restarted with the tested source; verified metadata survived that restart.
Capture was left stopped following offload testing until the operator re-arms.

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.text: Back to [the manager's README](../README.md).

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Teleprompter: scripts read to camera, followed word by word
sections.text:
The **Teleprompter** page (Show group, `camera_manager/prompter.py`) holds scripts for whoever speaks to camera, shown
large on a tablet beside it, the word being said lit as it is said, karaoke style, and kept at a reading line a third of
the way down. It is for the administrator and operators, and, on the camera network, for a tablet with nothing but the
teleprompter's own **PIN** at `https://teleprompter.mcvsaid.local` (port 8445 otherwise, `teleprompter_port`).

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Teleprompter: scripts read to camera, followed word by word
sections.text:
- **Scripts** are written on the page as text with a line `## Its title` for each section, kept in `teleprompter.json`
  beside the settings. A section is one of three kinds: **read** (said word by word, and followed), **lyrics** (`[lyrics]`
  after the title: a song, its line lit as it is sung) or **notes** (`[notes]`: points to speak from, never followed;
  ▼ moves to the next point). *New script* starts with sections suited to the kind of event.
- **By the kind of event.** Cooking has a script of its own, *The recipe*: a section for each step, its concise wording
  first, kept on the recipe's step however the step moves (the Recipe page, a spoken cue), and its Next and Back move the
  recipe as the Recipe page's do; read to the end, a step is not left, as it is read and then cooked. Live music writes
  sections as lyrics unless told otherwise and starts with following off (sung words are heard least surely); worship,
  podcasts, panels, theatre and Creator Studio follow by voice from the start, with questions and sermon points as notes.
- **Following the voice** (*Follow*, `teleprompter_follow`) uses the speech already set up on the Sound page (Standard AI
  or above, speech on), listening while the teleprompter is open on a tablet or the dashboard. Each look at what has
  been said (about once a second while someone talks) is found in the script near the place: the last eight words, in
  order, passing over a word left out or one not in the script ("um"), a long word heard a little wrong, and numbers as
  words or digits. Two words found move it on; going back, or more than twelve words ahead, needs four, so a common
  pair ("and the") sends it nowhere. Between hearings the lit word moves on at the pace last heard, never more than
  three words past what was heard. Read to its end, a section goes on to the next. What is heard moves the place and is
  never kept, as everywhere speech is heard. The programme's sound is held a few seconds behind, so the page says so:
  for no wait, listen to a microphone or the speaker's camera's own sound (Sound page, *Listen to*).

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Teleprompter: scripts read to camera, followed word by word
sections.text:
- **The controls**, on the tablet and the page alike: the previous and next section, a line back or on, **Play** (moves
  on by itself at speed 1 to 10, about 110 words a minute at 4), Follow, and on the tablet larger and smaller words and
  **Mirror** for a teleprompter's glass (both kept on that tablet). Keys: Page Down / Page Up and the arrows for a line
  (what a page-turner pedal sends), Space for Play, N and P for a section. An Xbox controller: A play, LB / RB section,
  d-pad up / down a line, left / right speed, Y follow. The place is one, shared by every tablet and the page. The top of
  the tablet shows REC and the camera on air; it keeps the screen on while open.
- **The tablet.** *Offer the teleprompter to tablets on the camera network* (administrator, after a restart) makes a
  six-digit PIN, shown once; *Make a new PIN* or *Set this PIN* (6 to 8 digits; a shorter one set before
  that was asked still works) log the tablets out. Only the PIN's hash
  is kept. Logged in, a tablet can move the script and nothing else: no settings, recordings or cameras. Wrong PINs
  slow the tablet that sent them, as wrong passwords do (see [Security](SECURITY.md#who-can-log-in)).

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Karaoke night: a line of singers, the words lit as they are sung
sections.text:
**Karaoke night** is a kind of event of its own (`event_mode` `karaoke`, chosen under *Event* in the side bar): guests
sing one after another at the microphone, the words on a screen facing them. Its cameras are the **Singer**, a **Duet
partner**, the **Host / KJ**, the whole stage and the crowd; the director holds the singer through a verse, goes to the
crowd often as it sings along, and to the stage between singers. The **Karaoke** page (Show group, karaoke night only,
`camera_manager/karaoke.py`) runs the night.

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Karaoke night: a line of singers, the words lit as they are sung
sections.text:
- **The music is the venue's.** The track plays from the venue's own karaoke setup (a KJ laptop, a karaoke machine,
  the mixer); nothing here plays, keeps or sends a track.
- **Songs** are teleprompter scripts (see [Teleprompter](#teleprompter-scripts-read-to-camera-followed-word-by-word)): written or pasted on the Teleprompter page, named
  "Title – Artist", a `## Verse` or `## Chorus` line before each part. In karaoke night every section is lyrics and
  following the voice is on: the singer sings to the screen with no hand free. The words of a real song belong to its
  writers: type in only words the venue has the right to show.
- **The singer's screen** is the teleprompter's tablet page, at `https://karaoke.mcvsaid.local` as well as
  `https://teleprompter.mcvsaid.local`, behind the teleprompter's PIN, on a tablet or a TV facing the singer. Along its
  top, who is singing and who is next; the song's line is lit as it is sung. **Next singer** (also on the screen: key S,
  controller X) marks the song sung and puts the next singer's song up from the top. Between songs, with nobody singing,
  it shows who is up next and the QR code to sign up by.
- **Guests sign up from their phones**: the QR code (on the Karaoke page and the screen between songs) opens
  `https://karaoke.mcvsaid.local/join?code=…` on the camera network. A first name and a song from the list; no account,
  no login. The night's code, four letters, is in the address (or typed); a phone may have two songs in the line at once,
  and asking is rate limited per address (and wrong codes from everyone together: 200 in ten minutes, and no code is
  checked until they are ten minutes old). What a guest asks for waits for the host's **Approve** unless *I approve each
  one* is switched off (`karaoke_approve`); *Guests can sign up* (`karaoke_signup`) closes it. The guest's phone shows
  their place in the line, and when they are up.

sections.doc: Teleprompter and karaoke night
sections.title: Karaoke night: a line of singers, the words lit as they are sung
sections.text:
- **What is kept**: a first name, the song and its place in the line, in `karaoke.json` beside the settings. Where a
  guest signed up from is held only in memory, to stop one phone filling the line. **New night** clears the line and makes
  a new code, so earlier QR codes open nothing; a line older than 18 hours is cleared by itself. Nothing sung is kept,
  as everywhere speech is heard.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.text: What the Cooking kind of event adds. The other kinds of event are in [the director](DIRECTOR.md#kinds-of-event); voice shot calls, which the same listening hears, are in [Sound and voice](SOUND_AND_VOICE.md).

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: The kitchen
sections.text:
- **A kitchen.** In Cooking the food counts as much as the cook: the model is told to favour the host when they talk
  to the camera, the board while hands cut there, the stovetop while something is in the pan, the oven while its door
  is open, the mixer while it runs, and the plate at the end. The board, bowl and counter cameras zoom to the hands at
  work (whatever the usual zoom choice); the stovetop, oven and grill are framed by the model, since the person
  detector finds people, not pans. The Cameras page says where each station's camera is best put (the board from
  overhead, the oven low and to one side). Without a recipe loaded, while the programme records, **Mark recipe step**
  on the Show page (or the S key) asks what the step is and marks "Step N: …": in the cut log, as a comment on its shot in the EDL, as a markers
  EDL beside the recording (`<name>.steps.edl`, which DaVinci Resolve imports as timeline markers), and in
  `<name>.cameras.json` with where each step falls in every camera file.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: The recipe
sections.text:
- **A recipe to follow.** In Cooking the side bar has a **Recipe** page, under Show. Load the recipe there, from its
  web page (the schema.org Recipe data that recipe sites publish) or pasted as text. Some sites turn away any program
  that reads their pages (bot protection such as Akamai's); the dashboard then says so, and the recipe is pasted
  instead, with the page's address kept for the QR code. Only pages on the public web are read: an address on this
  computer, on the camera network or on any other private network is refused, wherever a page sends the loader on to.
  Each step is given a caption in the -ing form ("Dicing the
  onions") and the stations it has to be seen at (the board, the stovetop, the oven).
- **Preparation.** What is done before the cooking proper (weighing, chopping, preheating: *mise en place*) is a
  section of its own ahead of the method: from a pasted recipe under a heading such as *Preparation*, *Prep*, *Before
  you start* or *Mise en place*, and from a page whose schema.org data has a section so named. (A recipe whose only
  steps are under *Preparation*, as some sites call the method, has them as its method.) The director follows the
  preparation like any steps, with their own stations; *Show on screen* puts it in the recipe overlay and calls its
  steps out, or leaves it off screen; *Skip the preparation* skips what is left of it, done before the show.
- **Ingredients, equipment and the recipe as text.** *Equipment* (or *Tools*, *Utensils*, *You'll need*, …; a page's
  schema.org `tool`) is a list of its own beside the ingredients, never shown on screen or heard as an ingredient
  (2026-10-24: a coffee maker and grinder under *Equipment:* had come out as ingredients). Both are edited one to a line
  near the top of the Recipe page. **Edit as text**, beside the title, opens the whole recipe as text (title,
  Ingredients, Equipment, Preparation, Method) to change anything at once; saved, it is read as a pasted recipe is, and
  a step whose words are unchanged, or changed only a little, stays the same step with what it has had
  (`recipe.from_edited_text`); Undo puts it back.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Prep for the show
sections.text:
- **Prep for the show.** A published recipe is written to be read: a step can be a paragraph doing four things, too
  long for the card on screen and for the host to call out. **Make concise steps** (`/api/recipe/prep`,
  `recipe.concise`) rewrites the preparation and the method as short steps, one action each in about eight words at
  most ("Grind the beans"), a long step split into several; each keeps the words it came from as its `details`, and its
  concise wording as `short` (with `details_on_screen`, whether the details may pop up beside it on screen; the overlay
  reads these three). Where the director's model is set up (`director_ai_url`, `director_ai_model`) it is asked, for
  strict JSON, given `recipe_prep_timeout_seconds` (90) to answer; an answer that is not JSON, makes up or leaves out a
  step, puts the steps out of order or is not short is not used, and rules make them instead, the page saying why.
  The rules split each step at its sentences (and "then"), a sentence with nothing to do in it ("it takes about 20
  seconds") or a caution ("take care not to break the yolks") staying with its action, and say each from its first verb
  to the end of its clause (`recipe.short_for`). The first step made from one keeps its id, and so what it has had; a
  step split from it gets stations from its own words, or the whole step's. The result is shown beside the original,
  each concise step editable (its wording, details, and whether they may go on screen), until **Use these steps** loads
  it as an edit, which **Undo** takes back, or **Keep the original**. Under it, **Check the room** lists the camera that
  covers each step (what each camera was given to show, roles of its own included) and flags a step none covers, and
  **Rehearse** lists what the host can say for each: its number ("step three") and its concise wording and first clause
  as the quick spotter hears them (`speech.rehearsal`), each with a button that tries it as *Try a phrase* does. A
  step's concise wording is a call as its own words are, for Whisper (`speech.said_step`, two words of its own will do
  when both are said) and the spotter (`speech.recipe_phrases`). Edit steps changes a step's concise wording and
  details later too.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Managing the steps
sections.text:
- **Managing the steps.** The Recipe page lists every step, the one being cooked picked out, with when each began, how
  long it has run, and which of its stations have had their key shot (✓) or are still owed one (○). **Go to** any step,
  **Next** (or the S key), **Back**, mark a step **Done** or **Skip** it (or *To come again*), and **Undo** what was last
  done, whoever did it: a move, a mark, the director's own move or an edit. **Edit steps** turns the list into an editor,
  apart from the controls for cooking it: click a step's words to change them (with its caption and stations), drag a
  step onto another to take its place (or ↑ ↓, on a touch screen), move it between the preparation and the method,
  delete it, or *+ Add a step here* between any two; before the show or during it, each step keeping what it has had
  through an edit (`recipe.js` arrangedRow, the same `/api/recipe/edit` actions). The Show page keeps a line of it: the step now,
  how long it has run, Back and Next.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: The host's own recipe page
sections.text:
- **The host's own recipe page.** On the camera Wi-Fi, the host opens `https://recipe.mcvsaid.local` on a tablet or
  phone on the counter (see [Easy addresses](SECURITY.md#who-can-log-in)), with no login but for Record and Stop: the recipe loaded here, one step at a time in large type
  (its concise wording above its full words), the next step beneath, a **Start** timer for each time a step names
  ("boil for 3 minutes", "ten minutes", beeping and flashing when done, +1 minute), the ingredients and equipment to
  tick off, and every step listed. **The ingredients come first**: once a recording has started and until a step
  begins, with the page open (asked for in the last 15 s), its Step view is the ingredients, for the host to go over
  ("Tell everyone what goes in"), each ticked as the manager hears it named (`Speech.named`; not the dish's own name),
  whether or not its line is shown on the programme. When every one has been named the first step begins by itself,
  the preparation's if there is any (`by: 'ingredients'`, audited as `ingredients_named`), and the preparation's steps
  and then Step 1 follow as ever. "Prep step one" (or "step one"), "next step", the page's own button (which reads
  *Prep 1 ›*) and the operator begin it too, with the list finished or not; a step's own words do not, while the
  ingredients are gone over. An ingredient the manager does not hear named leaves the list unfinished: the step
  is then begun by one of those. `recipe_ingredients_first` set to false in the configuration switches it off. **Next** and **Back** (or a swipe, or the arrow keys), and tapping any step, move
  the director's place in the recipe as Next and Back here do, before Record too (`by: 'host'` in its history); its
  **On screen** buttons put the recipe card up (for `speech_recipe_seconds`, as "show the recipe" does) or away, and
  pop the step being cooked up ("Step 2 of 5" and its caption). It follows whatever moves the steps, every two
  seconds, keeps the screen awake, and keeps its ticks, timers, text size and Prompter on the tablet itself. Only the
  recipe's words grow with **A+** (to 1.8x, 2.4x in Prompter): the header, tabs, timers and the buttons at the foot
  keep one small size, in one slim row (on a phone, Back is just ‹). **Prompter** (its button, or P) is the step
  alone for a host who reads it and says it in their own words: no tabs, a one-line header, the step's name and
  words as large as the text size makes them, the next step beneath, asked for every second; a new step flashes and
  says who moved it ("called out", "by the operator", "by the director"), and with spoken cues listening it says what
  to say, or that calling out moves the steps only once recording starts. `GET /api/kitchen` carries `moved` (the
  last move: `number`, `label`, `by`) and `voice` (`listening`, `steps`, `live`). Nothing else of the
  dashboard opens there: no loading, editing, marking, undoing or overlay settings. **REC** in its header says the
  programme is being recorded and for how long (red, counting), or *Not recording* (amber once a step has begun), and
  **● Record** and **■ Stop** at its foot do what the Director page's *Record programme to file* and *Stop* do. Those
  two want a login where nothing else on the page does: an operator or the administrator (the one login of the easy
  addresses, so logged in at `operate.` is logged in here; a setup tech is refused), asked for on the tablet the first
  time, and Stop asks first. `recipe_page_steps: false` leaves it following only, `recipe_page_screen: false` leaves
  the screen to the operator, `recipe_page_record: false` leaves the recording to the Director page (REC still shows).
  Also at `/kitchen` on the dashboard. `GET /api/kitchen` (with `recording`: `allowed`, `on`, `seconds`, `bytes`),
  `POST /api/kitchen/step` (`{"go": "next" | "back" | n}`), `POST /api/kitchen/screen` (`{"card": "show" | "hide"}`,
  `{"pop": true | n}`), from the page's own Origin only, and `POST /api/kitchen/record` (`{"record": true | false}`,
  logged in, with the CSRF token; audited as `kitchen_record`).

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: The director's following
sections.text:
- **The director's following.** With *The director moves on when it sees the next step*, the model is told the steps
  around the current one and says which it sees being worked on, the kitchen's sounds say which station is busy, and
  the next step still to come begins when they keep agreeing (only forward, one step at a time, skipping those done or
  skipped, and not before a step has had 20 s). The model is asked for this while a called or chosen shot is held too
  (only for the step: a hold is never cut by its ratings), and each look's step is in the recording's log. It is not
  told which step the cooking is at (told, it named that step every time), only the steps around it, and asked which
  step's action the pictures show happening. A step that names a camera's role of its own ("coffee maker", for a camera
  given *Coffee maker* under What it shows) has that camera as its station (`recipe.named`), so it is favoured and its
  key shot owed; calling that camera aloud when it is the next step's begins that step (`Tracker.called`); and while the
  host's gaze is choosing the shot (they look at the camera following them most of the time), the step's camera is still
  cut to for its key shot when the model rates it at least as well, and held 12 s (`Director.key_shot`); not while a cut
  the gaze chose is on its way, and never back to a camera the gaze took off air during the same step (the host turning
  to their camera to wrap up was cut away from). Said aloud,
  any step in its own words ("place the filter into the coffee maker": three quarters of its words, in a step of
  three or more) begins it, ahead or behind, the next step first, then the nearest (`speech.said_step`; not when
  denied), and any step's number does too, with no "moving on" ("step 2", "let's do step one", "and step two"; not
  "step 2 is where…" or "after step 2"). The words of the dish's name (the recipe's title) are not among a step's
  words, said in its own words, called out or gone to ("back to the…"): the name is said all through a show, and "So,
  cracker candy…" a minute in began the last step, *Let the cracker candy cool* (2026-11-16), which "let" and "cool"
  now say; a step with nothing but the dish's name in it is begun by its number or "next step". **While the
  ingredients are gone over**, a step's words begin nothing (`Speech.going_over`): read out, "a cup of salted butter,
  a cup of brown sugar" is most of the step that boils them, and it is the one stretch of a show where a step's words
  are said without the step being done. That is before the first step begins, and from a call of the ingredients' shot
  (a camera or a saved gimbal target called with "ingredients" in what was said) until another shot is called ("back
  to me"), a step begins, or two minutes pass. A step's number, "next step", the Recipe page's buttons, a phrase typed
  there and the operator begin a step all the same, so the first step is begun by "step one" or a tap, not by narrating
  it; ingredients named are still shown. The Heard list says when a step was held back, if the phrase did nothing
  else, and `speech_ingredients_hold` set to false in the configuration switches this off. A step **called out** in the host's own words, not the recipe's, begins it
  too, a step ahead only (`speech.called_step`, scored below a number or "next step"): led by a call ("now", "next",
  "let's", "time to", "okay", "alright", "so", "we're going to"…) in the first few words, with two of the words of
  its name (its concise wording and caption) said, near enough by stem ("let's get those peppers frying" for *Fry the
  pepper*, "alright, let's make our sauce", "okay, time to cover it and let it cook"), or one word only that step's
  name has and no ingredient's ("time to bake"). Not one ingredient alone ("now the garlic", "next up the eggs" stay
  the ingredient's lower third), not a step put off or talked about ("we'll bake it later", "before we crack the
  eggs", "once…", "after…"), and not one denied. The camera the model rates clearly
  best (by a point, and 6 or more), when it is the next step's station, counts as the model naming that step
  (`Tracker.seen_at`): three such looks begin it. Each look's decision is in the recording's log (`decisions`: the
  ratings with each lift, sound, star and recipe, and why it stayed or cut), and so are the gimbals' losses and findings. While a step is cooked its stations are favoured, strongly until each
  has been on air 12 s, so every step's key shot is captured; the dashboard says what is still to show and which steps
  were not shown long enough, and the cut log keeps what each step got and whether it was done or skipped. Each step
  that begins is marked in the recording as the operator's marks are.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Split screens in the kitchen
sections.text:
- **Split screens in the kitchen.** The model asks for a split when two things are both *changing* (hands at work,
  food stirred, poured or bubbling), never a dish or tray sitting untouched. In Cooking a split is shown only when each
  of its cameras has a station the step being cooked uses, or is the host's camera (`cook_host`); a camera given no
  station, or a step with none, is not held to it. Nor when one camera's picture has hardly changed for ten seconds
  (`stillness.py`: each picture shrunk to 64×36 grey dots and compared with the one ten seconds before, the middle of
  the last three, below `director_split_still_change`, 1.5 of 255; 0 switches it off; needs Pillow or OpenCV, as
  installed with the people packages, and without them nothing is measured). Measured on a real recording: a tray
  nobody touched changed by about 0.5, a pan boiling by about 3, hands at work by 10 to 50. A split stays up at most
  `director_split_max_seconds` (30 in Cooking, no limit otherwise, so a duet can last a song), or the *move on after
  at most* of the Director page when that is shorter; then it gives way to the better of its cameras and is not taken
  again for `director_split_rest_seconds` (30). A look away by the host that comes back to the split within 10 s does
  not restart its time, and the gaze never goes back to a split that may no longer be shown. A split on air leaves at
  once when the step moves away from one of its cameras. Each refusal is in the recording's log (`decisions`: "no
  split: Pixel shows counter, which Step 2 does not use"). (2026-11-15: a pot boiling beside an untouched tray of
  crackers held a split 5 min 48 s, 39% of the recording, because the model said "together" at every look.)

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: What goes on screen
sections.text:
- **When the recipe shows.** Under *When the recipe shows* on the Recipe page: **Always** (the whole show, as the old
  recipe switch, `overlay_recipe`, had it), **At moments** (`overlay_recipe_when` `moments`: for a while after Record
  starts, as each step begins, and after the last step is done, each a tick box, `overlay_recipe_moments`, for
  `overlay_recipe_moment_seconds`, 20 s by default, timed as the programme shows them), or **Only when asked** (the
  cook's "show the recipe", or **Show recipe**). **Show recipe** / **Hide recipe** (R) puts it up for 30 s or away now
  whichever is chosen, as the cook's "show the recipe" and "hide the recipe" do: always, it stays away until shown again;
  at moments, a showing is cut short until the next moment. On the card each step is in its concise wording when it has
  one (`short`, from the Recipe page's preparation for the show), and a long step without one is shortened at a clause.
  *Show each step's details when it pops up* (`overlay_step_details`, off by default) adds a step's details under its
  caption in the pop-up: its `details`, or else its full words when they are long; each step can say otherwise under
  its *More › Details when it pops up* (`details_on_screen`). With details off the pop-up is its label and caption.
- **On screen.** **Show recipe** (R) puts the whole recipe up beside the cook, on the side of the picture away from them,
  the current step picked out, using the whole height of that side (the preparation folds away once it is done and the
  method is under way; a recipe still too long is set smaller, but never too small to read, then shows a run of whole
  steps from the one before the step being cooked, never one cut through, with a line saying what is left out: "⋯ 7
  steps before", "⋯ 5 more steps"); captions, the pop-up and an ingredient's line wrap rather than cut off, so a step is
  read whole; **Show QR code** (Q) puts up a QR code of the
  recipe's address with "Get the recipe", in the lower corner on the other side, under the cook; each
  step is called out as it begins ("Step 3 · Braising the beef") and when the programme comes back to it after a while
  ("Braising the beef, continued"). For a few seconds a step can be **popped up** ("Step 2 of 6", its caption and, with
  details on, its details: the step's *More › Pop up on screen*, or the cook's cue), on the side away from the cook, and an ingredient
  the cook names is shown as a **lower third** at the foot of the programme on the cook's side, just above the QR code
  when it is up ("2 cups all-purpose flour"). It is a page laid over the programme by a browser source that **Add the
  overlay to OBS** puts on top in every programme scene, once; *Preview the overlay* opens the page in a browser tab.
  The page loads itself again when a new manager brings new overlay files, and the manager watches that OBS keeps
  asking for it: a browser source that failed to load the page (the manager restarting just then) shows nothing and
  never asks again, so after 20 s of silence OBS is told to reload it, and the Recipe and Show pages say so until it is
  showing again. The recipe on the page (its steps, pop-ups, captions and lower thirds) is shown as late as OBS shows the
  cameras, so a step begun as it is said comes up as it is said in the programme, not seconds before
  (`overlay_follow_programme`, at most `overlay_max_lag_seconds` 10); the director's captions are not delayed.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Spoken cues
sections.text:
- **Spoken cues** (optional, at the Standard and Plus AI levels). What the cook says moves the recipe on and puts things
  on screen, each cue switched on or off on the Recipe page. They work alongside the director, not instead of it: the
  director keeps choosing every shot (and following the steps, when set to), and a cue changes only the step and what
  is laid over the programme, where what the cook calls out takes precedence:
  - "let's see that recipe" (or "here's the recipe", "show you the full recipe"): the recipe for 30 s, with its QR code
    when it has an address;
  - "hide the recipe" (or "put the recipe away", "take the recipe down", "take the recipe off", "close the recipe"):
    the recipe put away now, whenever it is up ("don't hide the recipe" and "close the recipe book" do nothing);
  - "right now we're on step two" (or "step 2 now", "on to the third step", "prep step one", "next step", "let's move
    on", "moving on to the sauce"), and back or anywhere ("let's go back a step", "the previous step", "back to step 2",
    "let's revisit step 1", "back to the garlic", "jump to the eggs", "the final step"): that step begun, forward or
    back, and popped up on screen. The step after the one being cooked is never held back as "said again too soon" by a
    step just begun; any other step rests 4 s after one. The step expected next, said in its own words, needs only 60% of
    them when every word that tells it from the step being cooked is said ("start the copy maker" for "Start coffee
    maker", but not "add the water to the coffee maker"); any other step, three quarters. A camera called aloud begins
    the next step only once the step being cooked has run 10 s (`director_recipe_call_min_seconds`): "…into the coffee
    maker", a second into step three, began step four. Being the one expected, it is also taken on a less sure hearing
    (`speech_next_step_min_confidence`, 0.4, against 0.6 for any other cue). A step named by its words is the nearest that has them ("back to the garlic" is the
    last garlic step behind); when no step has them, an ingredient named is shown instead;

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Spoken cues
sections.text:
- an ingredient on the list named ("…two cups of flour…"): its line as a lower third for 6 s. Called out ("okay, now
    to our butter", "next up, the eggs", "here's the feta", "back to the butter"), it is shown again even if it just
    was; named in passing, it rests.

sections.doc: Cooking: the kitchen, the recipe and spoken cues
sections.title: Spoken cues
sections.text:
Speech is recognised **on this computer**, by Whisper run by faster-whisper, from the programme's sound (the tap
  that listening for instruments hears: the cook's microphone monitored to it in OBS) or a microphone chosen from the
  computer's own sound inputs under *Listen to* (the manager lists them, a minute apart: `host.sound_inputs`), or a
  camera's own microphone, live from the camera relay's copy of its stream (`camerasound.py`: about a third of a second
  behind real life, not held back with the programme; needs the relay on);
  nothing is sent anywhere, and what was heard is kept in memory only, the last ten phrases for the Recipe page, never
  saved. *Whisper small.en* is the default: on an M5 Pro Mac it takes about 0.75 s a phrase on the processor beside the
  vision model on the graphics, with neither slowed; *base.en* takes a third of that, for a smaller computer; with an
  NVIDIA card and CUDA set up it runs there. **How soon:** a phrase ends at a half-second pause, but a short command
  ("Bring it in") is looked at on the first breath (0.2 s of quiet); while someone talks on without one, what they have
  said so far is transcribed about once a second and a call or cue in it acted on at
  once (the rest of the phrase goes on from after it, so nothing is acted on twice); the Heard list says how long each
  took to understand. Through the programme's sound it is also as far behind as the programme runs (each camera's sync
  delay in OBS and OBS's monitoring, plus any look-ahead hold: at a 5.5 s hold, every call is acted on 5.5 s late), and
  the voice panel says so in red; choosing the host's own microphone under *Listen to* takes that away. Its set-up steps (install faster-whisper, download the model, hear the
  cook) are in **AI assistance** on the Director page, shown once spoken cues are switched on. To keep from acting on
  what was not meant, a cue needs a clear phrase, not a word in passing ("step 2 is where it gets tricky", "in the next
  step", "this recipe was my grandmother's", "don't show the recipe" do nothing); numbers may be words or digits; an
  ingredient whose name is shared (black pepper and a red pepper) needs the word that tells them apart; how sure the
  recogniser was times how clear the phrase is must reach 0.6 (`speech_min_confidence`); and each cue rests a while
  before it is acted on again (a step 10 s, any step 4 s, the recipe 20 s, an ingredient 45 s, or 2 s when called out). The Recipe page lists
  what was heard and what each phrase did or why it did nothing, and **Try a phrase** acts on one typed as if the cook
  said it, to see what a phrase would do. The same listening hears **voice shot calls** ([Sound and voice](SOUND_AND_VOICE.md#voice-shot-calls)): "cut to the stove"
  puts the stovetop camera on air, and a phrase that calls a camera is acted on as a call, not as a recipe cue.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.text:
Status: **phase 2 built** (design agreed 2026-10-17). Phase 1 chose and measured the keypoint model. Phase 2 adds the
kind of event, the framing editor on the Cameras page, the director's wiring, the consent gate and the readiness checks
(see *Phase 2: what is built* at the end).

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Creator Studio on the dashboard
sections.text:
**Creator Studio** is for one or a few people recording themselves, and nothing in it is preset: *build your own:
define the framings each camera follows, how close it shoots, and when it cuts.* Its panel is at the top of the Cameras
page (the administrator's):
- **Framings.** Each one goes from one body region to another (head, shoulders, elbows, hands, hips, knees, feet), with
  any others added and room around it, under a name you choose. A new set-up starts with five examples you can change
  or delete. *Preview* draws everyone's body keypoints and each framing on a camera's current picture.
- **The framing a camera shows**, chosen by anyone who runs the show (administrator or operator), at the top of its
  card's *What it shows* and on each Operate tile (`shows.js`, the same setting): *Whole person* or one of the framings,
  shown **alone** (`creator.favour` sets `only`, `POST /api/cameras/{id}/framing`): no other framing, and not the face
  or the whole person. Out of shot a moment, the shot and a gimbal's aim stay where it last was (`Director.framing_held`)
  until it is back or something else is chosen; the cut rules still see it gone. The set-up's own list of framings
  (first in shot, else the whole person) is kept for when *Whole person* is chosen again. **Or by voice:** each framing's name
  is a call ("give me the hands", or just "Hands!"), for the camera on air or the one just called, heard as your own
  phrases are (word for word, 50% sure) and by the quick phrase spotter; the director holds the shot meanwhile.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Creator Studio on the dashboard
sections.text:
- **Each camera** (its card's *What it shows*) favours the framings you pick, in order: the first in shot is framed,
  and the whole person when none is. You also set how close it shoots (tight, medium, loose), whom it follows when
  several people are in shot (by position only), and its own shot length if you want one. **A gimbal phone aims at the
  framing** (app 0.9.43): it follows faces, so for a framing that leaves the face out (Hands) the director tells it, from
  each look's keypoints, where the framing is from the face (`creator.aim`, `Director.aim_at_framing`), and it holds the
  face as high as the whole head allows so the framing comes to the middle; the crop does the rest.
- **When it cuts.** Shortest and longest shot, in turn or at random, cutting away when a camera's framing goes out of
  shot, and cutting to a camera when its framing comes into shot. A cut by hand, or from Stage Shots, always works.
- **Everyone on camera.** List everyone who will appear. Cameras do not arm or record, and the programme does not
  record or stream, until each person has consented and is confirmed as 18 or over. The record keeps who confirmed it
  and when. Pictures still reach this computer, so the framings can be set up.
- **On this computer only.** Framing uses a body keypoint model (MoveNet, Apache-2.0) beside the person detector, both
  from AI assistance at Plus. The vision model is off in this kind of event unless you turn it on, and then it only
  rates shots. No stills are kept with recordings, and nothing goes to the improvement store.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Creator Studio on the dashboard
sections.text: Measurements and design: [What it is](#what-it-is) and the sections after it.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: What it is
sections.text:
A new kind of event beside live music, worship, podcast, panel and theatre (`camera_manager/modes.py`, PR #108). It is for
one or a few people recording themselves: fitness, dance, beauty, demonstrations, or anything else. It is general purpose
and has no presets for any particular kind of content. The selector says:

> **Creator Studio.** Build your own: define the framings each camera follows, how close it shoots, and when it cuts.

Everything is the user's to define:
- **Framings.** Each is named freely and built geometrically from body regions, for example "head and shoulders",
  "from the hips to the knees", "hands", "full body", or a span between any two regions with padding.
- **Which cameras favour which framing.**
- **How close each camera shoots.**
- **When it cuts and how fast.**

A new set-up starts with five neutral examples (Full body, Head and shoulders, Upper body, Hands, Legs and feet). The user
can rename, change or delete each one.

The other kinds of event rely on the vision model (VLM) to rate shots. This one doesn't. Its framing comes from a small
keypoint model on this computer. The VLM stays optional and **off by default** for this kind of event. Cutting is by
rotation, by hand, or from Stage Shots.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
**Test material.** The S23 walk-by from recording 2026-10-16 11-27-40 (programme 225 to 291 s, file 266 to 333 s). One
person walks towards the camera, turns and crosses the picture. It was extracted at 10 pictures a second at the relay's
640 x 360. The person detector (yolox_s, 0.5) finds the walker in 114 of the 670 pictures. In 82 of those the whole body
is in the picture (from picture 226 on). Before that the walker is close to the camera with only the head at the bottom
edge. No other recording has people in it (docs/PEOPLE_LIBRARY.md).

**Method.** Every candidate is top-down: the person detector's box is cropped and handed to the keypoint model. Apple's
built-in Vision body pose and MoveNet MultiPose look at the whole picture instead, and are matched to the box. With no
hand-labelled truth available, two measures are used:
1. **Agreement with a reference:** RTMPose-m run on the same moments in S23's own **4K** file. This is the strongest
   model measured, with 6 times the pixels.
2. **A look at each result by eye:** 24 evenly spaced pictures, skeletons drawn on each.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Candidates
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
| Model | Licence of code and weights | Latency per person at 640 (median, p95) | Agreement with reference (within 10 % / 20 % of height) | By eye, 16 whole-body pictures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MoveNet SinglePose Thunder** (LiteRT, processor) | **Apache-2.0** (Google); trained on COCO and Google's own fitness, yoga and dance footage | **4.4 ms (4.8)**; 5.1 ms with JPEG decoding | **0.94 / 0.97** | 16 right |
| MoveNet SinglePose Lightning | Apache-2.0 (Google) | 1.9 ms (2.0) | 0.91 / 0.96 | 16 right; less sure of wrists |
| MoveNet MultiPose Lightning (whole picture) | Apache-2.0 (Google) | 13.7 ms (15.9) | 0.83 / 0.88 | 16 plausible; wrists and an ankle often missed |
| RTMPose-m, body7 (ONNX Runtime, Core ML) | Code Apache-2.0. Weights trained on body7, which includes **Halpe (non-commercial only)**, AI Challenger and PoseTrack | 3.3 ms (3.5); 12.4 ms on the processor | 1.00 / 1.00 (same model, so not independent) | 16 right |
| RTMPose-s, body7 | as RTMPose-m | 2.7 ms (2.9) | 1.00 / 1.00 | 16 right |
| Apple Vision body pose (built into macOS) | Part of the OS; Mac only | 5.5 ms (5.9) | 0.66 / 0.79 | legs merged or swapped in 5 side views |

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Candidates
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
By body region, MoveNet Thunder against the reference: head 0.90, shoulders 0.98, elbows 0.96, wrists 0.99, hips 0.99,
knees 0.93, ankles 0.94. On 1280 px pictures of the same moments it reaches **0.98**. So most of the gap at 640 comes
from the walker being only 70 to 100 pixels tall, not from the model. People recording themselves are nearer and larger
in the picture. MoveNet's model card says it is made for one person at 1 to 2 m (3 to 6 ft) from the camera, moving fast,
in fitness and dance.

**Edge of the picture.** In the 8 pictures with only the walker's head in shot, the models sometimes report shoulders
and arms that aren't there: RTMPose-m in 2, RTMPose-s in 6, MoveNet Thunder in 1. Lightning puts a stray triangle on the
face in 1. `pose.points` drops any keypoint outside the picture or below 0.3 confidence, whatever the model.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: How steady the framings are
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
For each example framing: how much its centre wobbles from one picture to the next, at 10 pictures a second. This is
the second difference, which removes steady movement, as a share of the person's height. It is measured over the 82
whole-body pictures, with the number of pictures the framing could be shown in:

| Framing | MoveNet Thunder | MoveNet Lightning | Reference (RTMPose-m) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full body | 4.2 % (72/82) | 5.1 % (72) | 3.0 % (73) |
| Head and shoulders | 2.4 % (80) | 2.5 % (80) | 2.0 % (79) |
| Upper body | 3.2 % (80) | 3.6 % (80) | 2.4 % (79) |
| Hands | 6.5 % (70) | 8.4 % (64) | 3.4 % (80) |
| Legs and feet | 4.9 % (72) | 4.7 % (72) | 3.4 % (74) |

The director's zoom already eases and holds, so a few percent of wobble does not show. Hands are the least steady
framing. Phase 2 adds a light smoothing filter on the keypoints (one-euro) and keeps the zoom's ease.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Recommendation
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
**MoveNet SinglePose Thunder**, 12.6 MB, run with LiteRT on the processor, top-down from the person detector's boxes:
- 4.4 ms a person, so five people take 22 ms beside the detector's 11 ms, well inside the 0.1 s fast-zoom tick.
- It matches the reference on 94 % of keypoints at 640 px and 98 % at 1280 px.
- Its licence and training data are clear for this use.
- LiteRT is already the instrument listener's runtime (`requirements-audio.txt`). It runs the same on the Linux
  workstation.

Lightning (1.9 ms) is the fallback for a slow computer. RTMPose is a little better and runs on Core ML, but its
published weights are not used because of their training data. This is the same reason the person re-identification
models were excluded (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Ultralytics' pose models are AGPL-3.0 and also not used. Apple Vision is
too often wrong about legs side-on, and it is Mac only.

**Not measured here:**
- Several people close together, and people lying down or seated. One walker is all the recordings have.
- Accuracy against hand-labelled truth. The agreement above is with the strongest model at 4K, which can itself be wrong.

Phase 2 starts with a short recording of consenting people from the team, standing, seated, turning and close
together. The same bench is run on it before the defaults are set.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: The kind of event
sections.text:
`modes.py` gets a sixth mode, `'creator'`, named **Creator Studio** (short: *Studio*), with the description above. What
makes it different from the other modes:
- **No fixed roles.** What each camera can be given to show is the user's own framings, not a list of roles.
  `modes.OFFERED['creator']` is empty and the Cameras page offers the framings instead.
- **The VLM is off by default.** `director_ai_enabled` is ignored in this mode unless the user turns on
  `creator_vlm` for this location. When it is on, it only rates shots. It never frames, and it never sees a framing's
  name.
- **No sound cues.** `SPEAKING` and `MUSIC` are both off.
- **Pace:** cut by rotation with 6 to 20 s shots until the user sets their own (see *When it cuts*).
- **Coordination:** the cooking-event session is also adding a mode to `modes.py`, so phase 2 rebases onto it.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: The framing editor (Cameras page → "What it shows", this mode only)
sections.text:
**Framings** are one list for the location:
- name (free text, up to 40 characters)
- **from** a region and **to** a region: head, shoulders, elbows, hands, hips, knees or feet. Every region in between
  is included.
- **also:** any other regions to keep in shot
- padding (0 to 50 % of the person's height)

A live preview from the chosen camera's newest picture draws the keypoints and the framing's box as it is edited. Up to
24 framings. Stored in the location's config as `creator_framings`. `pose.validate` checks each one.

**For each camera:**
- **Framings it favours**, in order. It shows the first one in shot and falls back to the next.
- **How close**: tight, medium or loose (padding × 0.6, 1, 1.6), or a fixed zoom.
- **Whom it follows** when several people are in shot: the largest person, the leftmost or rightmost, or the person
  nearest the centre. Positions only: nobody is identified.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: How the director uses it
sections.text:
In the fast follow loop (`director.follow_loop`, docs/PEOPLE_LIBRARY.md *Phase 2, step 1*), for a camera in this mode:
1. The person detector finds people. `pick` keeps to one by position, as now.
2. `pose.Keypoints` runs on that person's box (about 5 ms), smoothed over time.
3. `pose.region(keypoints, framing)` gives the box for the camera's first framing in shot. It replaces the fixed
   proportions of `director.focus` (`FOCUS`).
4. `framing()` turns it into the crop, as now: least 720 rows, ease, hold and room ahead of movement.

When none of a camera's framings is in shot, it shows the whole person. If nobody is found, it shows the whole picture.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: When it cuts
sections.text:
These are the user's settings, saved per location:
- **Rotation**: shortest and longest shot. The user can set a different time for each camera.
- **Order**: in turn, or at random among the cameras with their framing in shot.
- **Cut away when a camera loses its framing** (on by default), after a set number of seconds.
- **Cut to a camera when its framing comes into shot** (off by default).
- **By hand, or from Stage Shots:** always available. A cut by hand holds for the shortest shot before rotation
  takes over again.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Consent from everyone on camera
sections.text:
This reuses the performer library (`performers.py`, docs/PRIVACY_PERFORMER_LIBRARY.md):
- **Who is on camera.** Before recording, the user lists the people who will appear. They are chosen from the library
  or added there.
- **What each person needs.** The library's show consent, plus a new **"18 or over" confirmation**. That confirmation
  is required, and records who confirmed it and when (`consent['adult'] = {'confirmed': True, 'by', 'recorded',
  'date'}`). It is added through `performers.consent_record`, with the same withdrawal and deletion as the other
  records.
- **Arming is blocked** until every person on the list has both records. The cameras won't record or go live in this
  mode until then, and the dashboard says who is missing what.
- **The wording.** The dashboard shows one neutral sentence: *"MCVSAID can't verify anyone's age; it records who
  confirmed it and when."* There is no other notice.
- **No reference pictures needed.** People do not have to be enrolled with reference pictures, and recognition stays
  off unless the user turns it on as in any other mode.
- **More people than listed.** While armed, if the person detector sees more people in shot than are on the list,
  readiness warns (below).

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Local only
sections.text:
- **No cloud processing.** The keypoint model and the person detector run on this computer, and nothing is sent
  anywhere. The VLM, when the user turns it on, is the local model server, as in every mode.
- **Frames from this mode** are never written to the improvement store (`ImprovementStore` refuses them while the mode
  is `creator`). They are not kept as `.looks/` stills. They are left out of the diagnostic and crash bundles and
  location and fleet exports by default. Each exclusion gets a test.
- **Recordings** stay where the user's recordings always go. They are the user's own.
- **Framings** are geometry and names the user chose. They go with the location like its other settings.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Face blur
sections.text:
Face blur is **experimental** and hidden unless an administrator switches it on (System › This PC › Experimental
features; docs/FACE_BLUR.md): it may miss faces, especially small, turned or fast-moving ones, so Creator Studio does
not rely on it. With the switch off (the default), Creator Studio neither shows nor applies it, and AI assistance offers
none of its steps. With it on, this kind of event starts at **every face** with the **fail-safe**, as below, changeable
on the Director page. An installation already in Creator Studio when the switch was added starts with it on, once, so
that the update does not silently stop blurring.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Readiness and set-up
sections.text:
AI assistance (PR #105) gets a step for this mode: **"Body regions: the keypoint model (MoveNet Thunder, 12.6 MB)"**, with
a **Download** button. It is fetched into `<data>/people/movenet_thunder.tflite` from
`https://tfhub.dev/google/lite-model/movenet/singlepose/thunder/tflite/float16/4?lite-format=tflite` and checked against
SHA-256 `41641538679ec79b07d4101e591dda47d098c09af29607674b2a40b8a3798dd3`. It is used without a restart. The step also
needs the person detector (already a Plus step) and ai-edge-litert (already the listening step's runtime).

Readiness warnings in this mode:
- Someone on the list lacks show consent or the 18-or-over confirmation. Cameras won't arm until this is fixed.
- More people in shot than are listed (the detector's count, while armed).
- The keypoint model or the person detector is missing. Framings fall back to the whole person until it is installed.
- A camera favours a framing that no longer exists.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Phase 2 tests (in the existing styles, neutral fixtures)
sections.text:
- `test_modes.py`: the mode is offered with its description. The VLM is off by default in it. Its pace applies.
- The framing editor's API: validation, at most 24 framings, the administrator only, and the operator gets 403.
- The director: a camera's first framing in shot is framed (stand-in keypoints). It falls back to the next framing,
  then to the whole person. Rotation and cut-away timings work.
- Consent: arming is refused until everyone listed has show consent and the 18-or-over confirmation. The record holds
  who and when. Withdrawing it disarms. The readiness warning appears when more people are seen than listed.
- Local only: nothing from this mode reaches the improvement store, `.looks/`, diagnostic bundles or exports.
- Face blur in this mode: left out while the experimental switch is off; every face with the fail-safe once it is on.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: What is in this pull request
sections.text:
- `camera_manager/pose.py`: framings as geometry between body regions (`validate`, `groups`, `points`, `height`,
  `region`, neutral `EXAMPLES`) and the keypoint model (`Keypoints`, MoveNet through LiteRT, top-down from the
  detector's boxes). It is not used by anything yet.
- `tests/test_pose.py`: framings from a made-up standing figure, regions out of shot, keypoints that aren't sure,
  validation, and the model itself when it is installed.
- `tools/pose_bench.py`: the measurements above, reproducible (`keypoints`, `compare`, `steady`).
- `requirements-people.txt`: ai-edge-litert. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: the keypoint model.

Reproducing the tables, from a checkout, with the walk-by pictures extracted by ffmpeg:

```
python tools/pose_bench.py keypoints <data>/people/yolox_s.onnx movenet_thunder.tflite f640 thunder.json
python tools/pose_bench.py keypoints <data>/people/yolox_s.onnx rtmpose-m/end2end.onnx f640 rtmpose.json
python tools/pose_bench.py compare rtmpose.json thunder.json
python tools/pose_bench.py steady thunder.json 226
```

(The 4K reference was taken with the prototype on the same moments; `keypoints` on a folder of 4K pictures gives it too.)

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Phase 2: what is built
sections.text:
- **The kind of event** (`modes.py`): `'creator'`, *Creator Studio* (*Studio*), with the description above. No roles;
  no sound cues; cameras in turn, 6 to 20 s, zoomed. `modes.vision_model` keeps the VLM off here unless
  `creator_vlm` is on (`chooser.Advisor.enabled`).
- **Settings** (`creator.py`, saved in the location's config and carried with its settings, except the list of people):
  `creator_framings`, `creator_cameras` (favoured framings, closeness, whom to follow), `creator_cuts`, `creator_people`,
  `creator_vlm`.
- **The Cameras page** (`static/creator.js`, the administrator's): *Everyone on camera* (add someone with both
  confirmations, or from the library, confirm or withdraw the 18-or-over confirmation, take someone off the list), the
  framing editor, *Preview* (`POST /api/creator/preview`: the camera's current picture with everyone's keypoints and
  each framing; the picture is not kept), and *When it cuts*. Each camera's *What it shows* has its favoured framings,
  how close it shoots, whom it follows and its own shot length. An operator sees that the administrator set it up.
- **The director**: in the fast follow loop, the person the camera follows (taken by the user's position rule, then
  kept by position) gets keypoints, and `creator.framing_for` gives the box of the first favoured framing in shot,
  scaled by closeness. When no framing is in shot it shows the whole person, as it does without the keypoint model.
  The cutting rules are `Director.studio_cut` and `studio_choice`: cut away after `lost_seconds` without the framing,
  cut to a camera whose framing comes into shot (cameras off air are looked at in turn for this), never before the
  shortest shot, and in turn or at random. Each camera can have its own shot length. A cut by hand or from Stage Shots
  holds as in every mode.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Phase 2: what is built
sections.text:
- **The consent gate** (`Manager.studio_gate`): `camera.arm` and `recording.start` to the phones, and the programme's
  record and stream, get 409 with who is missing what. Streams to this computer are allowed, so the framings can be set
  up from live pictures. Already armed cameras are not disarmed when the mode is chosen; readiness then shows the
  failure. The 18-or-over record is `performers.Library.confirm_adult` / `withdraw_adult` (who and when). The audit log
  has labels, not names.
- **Local only**: the director keeps no `.looks` stills in this mode. `ImprovementStore` refuses pictures while it is
  chosen.
- **Readiness** (`system.studio_checks`): everyone listed confirmed, or who is missing what (fail); more people in shot
  in the last 10 s than are listed (warn); the person detector or the keypoint model missing (warn); a camera favouring
  a framing that no longer exists (warn).
- **AI assistance**: in this mode at Plus, the steps are the runtimes (ONNX Runtime and LiteRT), the person detector
  and the keypoint model (**Download**, pinned SHA-256). The VLM's steps appear only when `creator_vlm` is on. Below
  Plus, one step says framing needs Plus.
- **Face blur** (`faceblur.py`, #116; experimental since the switch was added): only while an administrator has
  switched experimental face blur on, this kind of event starts at *every face*, with the fail-safe blurring the whole
  picture when detection cannot keep up, until the administrator chooses otherwise on the Director page. The Creator
  Studio panel then says what is set, that it may miss faces, and links there, warning when it is not every face with a
  fail-safe. With the switch off, the panel says nothing of it and nothing is blurred.

sections.doc: Creator Studio: framings you build yourself from body regions (design, measurements, what is built)
sections.title: Phase 2: what is built
sections.text:
- **Tests**: `tests/test_creator.py` (mode, framings, cameras, cutting, the consent gate through the API, readiness, the
  preview, portability, the set-up steps, the director's framing and cutting, the VLM off, no improvement pictures)
  and `tests/test_pose.py`.

Not done yet:
- **Not tried on phones.** Neither the keypoint model nor the framings have run on phone pictures or with several people
  close together. That needs the rehearsal recording described above.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
