sections.title: The performer library (Plus AI)
sections.text:
At Plus, the director can recognise **consenting** performers (or speakers) and nobody else. Design:
[Design and measurements](#design-and-measurements), below; privacy rules and consent templates:
[docs/PRIVACY_PERFORMER_LIBRARY.md](PRIVACY_PERFORMER_LIBRARY.md) (not legal advice).

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: The performer library (Plus AI)
sections.text:
- **Enrolling** (Set up › People, administrator only): take a picture from a camera, and the person detector outlines the
  people in it; click one (or drag a box), give a name, a role (*Performer*, or *Star*: priority on any camera) and
  instruments, and add. Reference pictures are taken on the day, in what they perform in. Per performer: more pictures,
  the cameras that follow them, their improvement consent, and removal, which deletes their data.
- **Consent**, per purpose: recognising them during the show (needed), and helping improve MCVSAID (optional and
  separate). Adding a performer asks for one tick confirming their signed release, or nothing when the production has
  said once that consent is handled by contract. MCVSAID keeps only that consent was confirmed, by whom, when and on
  what basis; the releases themselves stay with the production.
- **Privacy.** Only a 160 px thumbnail and an appearance descriptor (and a face descriptor, where their release covers
  it) are kept, encrypted (AES-256-GCM, the key in the Keychain or Secret Service), and deleted at the end of the show
  day by default (at most three years). The picture a performer is enrolled from is held in memory for ten minutes.
  Logs and reports say "performer 2", never a name. Anyone not enrolled is never identified. Pictures kept to improve
  MCVSAID are pseudonymised, with everyone else in them blurred past recognition. **Delete all performer data** is on
  the same page.
- **While recognition is on**, every page (Stage Shots too) says **Performer recognition: ON**.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: The performer library (Plus AI)
sections.text:
- **The fast zoom.** A person detector (YOLOX-s, Apache-2.0, through ONNX Runtime; 11.5 ms a picture with Core ML on the
  M5 Pro) runs on a decoder kept running per followed camera, fed by the camera relay: a look every 0.1 s. Replayed on a
  recorded walk-by it followed the walker in 93 of 108 looks and followed nobody in 155 empty ones; the model's own locate
  had taken 4 to 6 s. A camera frames a performer it follows first, then a star, and never zooms in on someone not
  recognised. Stars seen in a camera's picture lift its rating.

- **Faces, with their own tick.** Where a performer's release also covers their face, a face clear enough (eyes at
  least 18 px apart, facing the camera, sharp) is used beside how they look: YuNet finds it and its landmarks, it is
  aligned and described by SFace (the Plus set-up downloads it), and the descriptors are kept encrypted with the rest
  and deleted with them. A clear, different face outweighs a matching costume. Per camera, a performer recognised a
  moment ago stays recognised while they turn away, for up to 3 s, and not when people cross. The People page shows
  each reference picture's face quality and warns about too few pictures, one camera only, or no clear face.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: The performer library (Plus AI)
sections.text:
Recognition accuracy with real performers is still to be measured at a consenting rehearsal
(`tools/recognition_eval.py`). On a synthetic set made from public-domain portraits (below), where a
face was clear, adding it took recognition from 23 % to 45 % of looks, wrong performers from 12.8 % to 0.1 % and
strangers taken from 21.7 % to 1.9 %; but the body alone at the shipped threshold took one stranger's look in five for
a performer, and faces are large enough in only 6 % of the follow loop's 640-wide pictures (17 % at 1280). Until the
rehearsal, treat stars and follow rules as unproven.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Design and measurements
sections.text:
Status: **phase 1, for agreement.** The detector, the encrypted consent-gated library, the matcher, the improvement
store with blurring, and their tests are here. Nothing is wired into the live director, the dashboard or the
cameras yet. Phase 2 does that once this design is agreed. Privacy is described in
[PRIVACY_PERFORMER_LIBRARY.md](PRIVACY_PERFORMER_LIBRARY.md). It is a requirement, not an option.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: What it is for
sections.text:
> "Would it be possible if the 'What it shows' section had a reference images feature? ... label who is who and have
> certain cameras follow certain folks or know who is important versus who might be in the crowd... Maybe have a star
> performers feature so certain folks are given primary tracking regardless of camera."

1. **Follow people fast.** The director's zoom asks the shot model (the VLM) where the person is. That takes 1.5 to
   2 s per answer and 4 to 6 s end to end live (2026-10-16), which is too slow to follow anyone moving. A small
   person detector answers in about 12 ms.
2. **Know who is who, with consent.** A library of consenting performers, each labelled as a performer or a star,
   with their instruments, reference pictures and follow rules. Stars get priority on any camera. Chosen cameras
   follow chosen performers. Everyone else is "unknown" and is never identified.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Person detector: YOLOX (Apache-2.0) through ONNX Runtime
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-16/17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
Latency per 640 px picture, median (95th percentile), over the 264 pictures of the S23 walk-by. The input is
letterboxed to the model's square.

| Model | Input | Core ML | Processor only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yolox_nano | 416 | 4.3 ms (4.7) | 8.4 ms (8.6) |
| yolox_tiny | 416 | 5.3 ms (5.6) | 15.8 ms (16.6) |
| **yolox_s** | 640 | **11.5 ms (12.5)** | 45.5 ms (47.1) |
| yolox_m | 640 | 16.7 ms (19.3) | 88.3 ms (90.0) |

Accuracy on the walk-by analysed on 2026-10-16: recording 11-27-40, S23's own 4K file, programme 225 to 291 s, at
4 pictures a second, scaled to 640 wide. Every picture was labelled by eye. The walker is in 53 pictures and
behind the tree in 12. The other 199 pictures are empty.

| | Walker found | Something found in an empty picture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yolox_nano, threshold 0.5 | 34 / 53 | 0 / 199 |
| yolox_tiny, 0.5 | 43 / 53 | 0 / 199 |
| **yolox_s, 0.5** | **47 / 53** | **0 / 199** |
| yolox_s, 0.3 | 48 / 53 | 4 / 199 (the red-leaved tree, 0.26 to 0.45) |
| yolox_m, 0.5 | 48 / 53 | 0 / 199 |
| The VLM's locate (`truth.json`, same frames, at its own pace) | 23 / 26 asked | 0 / 63 asked, median 2.0 s per answer, max 3.4 s |

yolox_s misses the walker only as they enter at the bottom edge of the picture and in one picture at 0.45. It
never boxes the litter bin that fooled the VLM on the phone's pictures. That is ~170 times faster per answer at
the same or better accuracy, so it can run at 5 to 10 looks a second.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Person detector: YOLOX (Apache-2.0) through ONNX Runtime
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-16/17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
Across all 4,551 stills in `~/Videos/Program/*.looks/` (6 recordings, threshold 0.25), the detector also boxes
**hands** in the desk and ceiling test shots (up to 0.8; COCO calls a hand "person") and the same **tree**
(up to 0.6 on the phone's sharpened stills). The director's existing checks deal with both kinds:
`plausible()` (least person height and shape) and the scenery memory (`is_scenery`). Phase 2 keeps both, with
threshold 0.5 by default.

**Recommendation:** yolox_s at 640, threshold 0.5, through Core ML on the Mac and CUDA on the Linux workstation.
yolox_tiny is the fallback for a computer without an accelerator (16 ms on the processor).

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Appearance matching: what these recordings can and cannot show
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-16/17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
All 14 minutes of every camera in 11-27-40 were scanned at 2 pictures a second. People appear on **one** camera
(S23): 25 pictures, all of **one** person, plus two tree false detections. The earlier recordings show only hands
at a desk. So the recordings can't measure accuracy across cameras or the false-match rate on strangers. Those
need people who have agreed to it (see *Before going live*). What they do show, enrolling the walker from three
back views and comparing the other 16 views (side, front, close up):

| Descriptor | Same person, other views (min / median) | Tree false detections |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DINOv2 ViT-S/14 + colour histogram (shipped default) | 0.52 / 0.72 | 0.42, 0.46 |
| DINOv2 only | 0.39 / 0.60 | 0.31, 0.35 |
| Colour histogram only | 0.69 / 0.85 | 0.58, 0.61 |

Describing people takes 7 ms each on the processor (28 ms for 4). Core ML is *slower* for DINOv2 here (100 ms for
4) because only part of the graph runs on it, so the processor is the default.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Appearance matching: what these recordings can and cannot show
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-16/17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
What this means:
- A general image model separates a person from scenery, but the same person from behind and from the front is
  far apart (0.52). At the conservative default threshold (0.75 and a 0.05 lead), most views of this walker would
  stay "unknown". That is the safe failure: the director just frames them as it does today.
- Recognition will rely on **references taken from each camera** at the show (the library keeps up to 8 per
  performer, tagged by camera) and on stage clothing. Performers mostly face the audience and stay in a known area
  of the stage.
- Phase 1 used no face model: off-the-shelf face embeddings (ArcFace, InsightFace) carry non-commercial terms. Faces
  were added later, for performers whose release covers them (*Faces, fusion and measuring recognition*, below).
  Person re-identification models (OSNet and similar) are excluded because of the terms of their training datasets
  (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

**The threshold is not set from these numbers.** Phase 2 starts with a consenting rehearsal measurement (below), and
the threshold and lead are set from its false-match rate on people left out of the library.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Blurring
trail: Phase 1 measurements (M5 Pro, 2026-10-16/17, with the live manager and model server running)
sections.text:
`persons.blur` pixelates each box (grown by 10 % on every side) to 3 blocks across and then smooths it. At the
walker's size (about 35 x 150 px at 640 wide) nothing of the person is recognisable, not even clothing colours. A
test checks that stripes inside a non-consenting person's box are gone after saving, and that a consenting
performer is left as they were.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Pipeline (phase 2)
sections.text:
```
relay (persistent decoder, followed camera only, 640 px, 5-10 Hz)
  -> persons.Detector (yolox_s, ~12 ms)                       positions only, no identity
  -> if recognition is ON: performers.Appearance on each box (~7 ms each, processor)
       -> performers.Matcher against the library (enrolled only; conservative; no state kept)
       -> descriptors dropped with the picture
  -> director: zoom target, star bonus, follow rules
VLM: keeps rating shots as now; no longer asked to locate when the detector is available.
```

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Pipeline (phase 2)
sections.text:
- **Relay pictures at 5 to 10 Hz.** `iso.newest_picture` now starts ffmpeg for each picture (about 0.4 s of
  processor, the director's note in `snapshot`), which is fine at one a second and not at ten. Phase 2 keeps one
  decoder running per *followed* camera (normally the one on air or about to be) that hands over the newest
  decoded picture. VideoToolbox decodes on the Mac and NVDEC on the workstation.
- **Locate.** `Director.find` calls the detector instead of `advisor.locate` when it is installed, and falls back to
  the VLM when it isn't. The answer has the same shape (a box), so the zoom, smoothing, hold, late-answer and
  scenery logic all stay as they are. With answers about 0.1 s old instead of 2 to 6 s, `director_zoom_every_seconds`
  can drop to 0.1 to 0.2.
- **Choosing whom to frame,** in order: a performer this camera follows, then a star, then the person the camera's
  focus asks for (lead singer, drummer and so on, as now), then the largest person. **Unknown people are never zoom
  targets** unless the camera's focus is the crowd, and then the crowd is framed as a whole.
- **Stars get priority regardless of camera.** `chooser` gives a camera a score bonus (`director_star_bonus`, default
  +1.5 on the model's 0 to 10 scale) while a star is recognised in its latest look. That camera wins ties and close
  calls but not an empty shot, so a star at the edge of a wide shot doesn't beat a good close-up.
- **Follow rules** live with the performer in the library (`set_follow(performer, [camera ids])`) and are shown on the
  camera's "What it shows" panel to the administrator only. A camera following someone keeps them as its zoom target
  and stays off the program while they are out of its shot, if another camera has them.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Pipeline (phase 2)
sections.text:
- **Between identity checks,** the zoom keeps hold of *its target's box* by overlap from one picture to the next,
  for a few seconds at most, so the zoom doesn't jump. This follows a position, not an identity, and is kept only
  for an enrolled performer. An unknown person's box is never carried from one picture to the next by identity.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Storage
sections.text:
| What | Where | Encrypted | Leaves the computer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Library (names, roles, references, consent, follow rules) | `<data>/people/library.bin` | AES-256-GCM, key in Keychain or Secret Service or a 0600 file | Never |
| Improvement store (pseudonymised items, withdrawn pseudonyms) | `<data>/people-improvement/store.bin` | Separately keyed | Only as an administrator's export, encrypted with a passphrase |
| Improvement audit trail (exports, withdrawals; pseudonyms and counts) | `<data>/people-improvement/audit.jsonl` | No (contains no names) | Never |
| Operational metadata (latency, cut timing, zoom error) | The usual logs and `.cuts.json` | As today | As today; never names |

The band profile keeps only the performer ids it uses (for follow rules). Names stay in the library.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Dashboard (phase 2, in the new layout from PR #99)
sections.text:
- **"What it shows" → People** (administrator only): *Take a picture* from a chosen camera, then click or draw the
  boxes the detector offers. For each box: name, role (performer or star), instruments. The **Purpose A consent
  record** is required (who gave it, who obtained it, date, scope, retention, release no.). **Purpose B** is a
  separate optional checkbox with its own record. Saving keeps a 160 px thumbnail and the descriptor. The rest of
  the picture is discarded.
- **Turn on recognition** for this show day or this location. The side bar then shows **Performer recognition: ON**
  on every page and for every role. Operators see only that, never names or pictures.
- **Delete** per performer, **withdraw** per purpose, **delete all performer data**, **export improvement data**
  (passphrase, audit entry).
- **Readiness:** recognition on with no consent records, data past retention, an export not yet confirmed as handed
  over.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Exclusions (phase 2, each with a test)
sections.text:
`people/` and `people-improvement/` are left out of location and fleet exports (`transfer.py`, `locations.py`),
release and update bundles, the diagnostic and crash bundles and the audit log. The director's recording log
(`locates`) and `.cuts.json` say "performer 2" or "unknown", never a name. No name goes into any prompt to the VLM.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Faces, fusion and measuring recognition (2026-10-17)
sections.text:
Built: `camera_manager/faceprints.py` (aligning, judging and describing a face), face descriptors in the library,
`performers.Matcher` weighing a face with the body, `performers.Identities` carrying a performer through a look where
they are turned away, the People page's reference quality and advice, a set-up step for the face model, and
`tools/recognition_eval.py`, which measures all of it. **Every number below is from a synthetic set, not from people
on a stage. Real numbers need the consenting rehearsal above.**

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: How a face is used
sections.text:
1. YuNet (already used by face blur, MIT) finds each face and its five landmarks. A face belongs to a person when it
   lies in the top 45 % of their box, or, where boxes overlap, of the one person it is clearly centred on.
2. The face is aligned to the standard 112 x 112 template from those five points (a similarity transform).
3. It is used only when it is good enough (`faceprints.GATES`): eyes at least 18 px apart in the picture looked at,
   turned sideways at most 0.32 eye spacings, tilted at most 0.45, sharp enough (Laplacian variance 40 on the aligned
   face), and a detector score of at least 0.6.
4. The face model gives a descriptor of unit length, compared by cosine with the performer's face references.
5. **Evidence** for a performer = (body similarity - `people_match_threshold`) + `people_face_weight` x (face
   similarity - `people_face_threshold`), where the person's face is usable and the performer has a face reference;
   otherwise the body alone, exactly as before. A match needs evidence of at least 0 and a lead of
   `people_match_margin` over the next performer. So a clear, different face outweighs a matching costume, and a clear
   matching face outweighs a costume seen from another side.
6. **Carried through the track** (`Identities`, per camera, from the director's follow loop): people are followed from
   look to look by box overlap. A performer named at least twice among the last six times anyone was named for that
   person, and twice as often as anyone else, stays named through looks where nothing is recognised (turned away), for
   up to `people_carry_seconds` (3 s) after the last time. When two people's boxes overlap, neither is carried until
   named again. For anyone never named, only a box and a time are kept, forgotten after a second.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: How a face is used
sections.text:
Only for performers whose release covers their face (one tick on enrolment, or the contract arrangement's
*also covers their faces*): for anyone else no face descriptor is kept and they are matched by the body alone.
*Stop using their face* on the People page deletes their face descriptors and keeps the rest. Face descriptors are in
the encrypted library next to the appearance descriptors, expire with them, and go when the performer does.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: The models (licences)
sections.text:
No face recognition model was found whose weights *and* training data are both documented as open to commercial use:

| Model | Weights | Training data | Size, time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **SFace** (OpenCV model zoo, `face_recognition_sface_2021dec.onnx`) | Apache-2.0 | **Not documented.** The SFace paper trains on CASIA-WebFace, VGGFace2 and MS1MV2, all collected from the web without the subjects' consent; CASIA-WebFace is for non-commercial research and MS-Celeb-1M was withdrawn. opencv_zoo issues #313 and #318 ask which; the only answer (Oct 2026) was that the Apache licence "should be clear enough" | 37 MB, 16.7 ms a face (median, processor) |
| **AuraFace v1** (fal, `glintr100.onnx`) | Apache-2.0 | "A commercial dataset comprising face images from various sources", not named or audited. Its weights differ from InsightFace's glintr100 (checked: same network, different weights), but the same repository also carries four of InsightFace's non-commercial files unchanged under the Apache label, which they are not | 249 MB, 138 ms a face (median, processor) |
| Excluded | ArcFace/InsightFace (non-commercial weights), EdgeFace (CC BY-NC-SA), AdaFace (no licence; MS1M/WebFace), models trained on DigiFace-1M (dataset non-commercial) or SynFace (FFHQ, non-commercial), FaceNet ports (CASIA, VGGFace2). dlib's model is public domain but trained on scraped data and is not ONNX. Apple's Vision has no face identity descriptor | | |

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: The models (licences)
sections.text:
`people_face_model` chooses (`sface`, `auraface`, or `off`). **SFace is the default** (chosen 2026-10-17): it is a
seventh the size and eight times faster than AuraFace, and as accurate here; its training data is the caveat above.
The Plus set-up downloads it and YuNet, each checked against a pinned SHA-256 (`faceprints.FACE_MODELS`,
`faces.YUNET`); `off` removes the step and uses no face at all.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Measured on a synthetic set (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17)
sections.text:
The recorded camera files have one distant walker and no faces, so the set was made: `recognition_eval.py synth`.
- **People:** 24 NASA astronauts, from public-domain portraits and mission photographs (images.nasa.gov), 3 to 11
  photographs each, 155 in all. Photographs with exactly one clear, roughly frontal face were kept, and then any
  whose face resembled none of the same person's others (captioned with their name, but someone else) were dropped,
  using SFace. Identities are codes (P01 to P24).
- **Scenes:** a real frame from each of six cameras of the 2026-10-16 recording, as background. Each person is a drawn
  figure in a costume, six of them all in black (a band dressed alike) and the rest each in their own. The head is
  cut from one of their photographs, another one on each camera as far as there are enough. Seven cameras: far (the
  person 0.25 to 0.3 of the picture's height), wide, balcony (darker, softer), side (bluer), medium, close (0.85 to
  0.95), and tight (from the waist up). Three people to a clip, walking across, sometimes crossing; seen from behind
  in a fifth of the looks. 112 clips of 8 looks, 2,688 person looks.
- **Asked:** 20 rounds; in each, 12 people drawn at random are enrolled from one look on each camera (facing it, the
  face clear where possible), and the other 12 are strangers. Every look not from a reference's clip is asked. A look
  showing the same photograph as one of the performer's references is left out: it would be too easy.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Measured on a synthetic set (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17)
sections.text:
What it does not show: real bodies, clothes, stage light, motion blur, real cameras' compression, profiles and
partly hidden faces. The figures are flat drawings, so the body numbers here say little about real performers; they
are what the matcher makes of costumes and the camera's background, which is itself a warning (below).

**Usable faces** (all gates passed), out of 2,688 looks:

| Picture looked at | Usable face | Why not, mostly |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 640 wide (the follow loop's `director_zoom_frame_width`) | 6 % | too small: eyes under 18 px in all but the tight and close cameras |
| 1280 wide (face blur's pictures) | 17 % | too small 1,020, turned away 576, not found or not in one person's head 402, blurred 222 |
| 1920 wide | 34 % | turned away 586, blurred 573 |

A whole person 0.9 of the picture tall has eyes about 25 px apart at 1280 wide, as on a real person; on a wide shot a
face is too small to tell anyone apart, whatever the model.

**Each signal alone and both together**, SFace, pictures 1280 wide. Recognised: of enrolled people's looks. Wrong
performer: of enrolled people's looks. Stranger taken: of strangers' looks (and, in brackets, of those where the
stranger's face was clear).

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Measured on a synthetic set (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17)
sections.text:
| | Recognised | Wrong performer | Stranger taken |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Body alone, 0.75 (the shipped threshold) | 29.1 % | 12.9 % | 20.1 % (21.7 %) |
| Body alone, 0.85 | 6.7 % | 5.3 % | 5.4 % |
| Body alone, 0.90 | 0.8 % | 1.7 % | 1.2 % |
| Face alone, 0.40 | 13.0 % | 0.7 % | 1.0 % (5.7 %) |
| Face alone, 0.50 | 9.6 % | 0.1 % | 0.4 % (2.1 %) |
| Both, body 0.75, face 0.55 x 1 (the defaults) | 33.1 % | 10.6 % | 16.9 % (1.9 %) |
| ... carried through the track | 35.3 % | 12.6 % | 19.6 % (4.6 %) |
| Both, body 0.95, face 0.30 x 1 (the safest found) | 9.5 % | 0.1 % | 0.3 % (1.3 %) |
| ... carried through the track | 10.5 % | 0.1 % | 0.3 % (1.6 %) |
| Same, 1920 wide (body 0.95, face 0.35) | 19.9 %, carried 22.3 % | 0.1 % | 0.4 % (1.0 %) |
| Same, 640 wide | 3.9 % | 0.0 % | 0.0 % |

**Where a face is clear**, with the body threshold left at 0.75 (the defaults: face 0.55, weight 1, SFace):

| Looks with a usable face, 1280 wide | Recognised | Wrong performer | Stranger taken |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Body alone, 0.75 | 23.2 % | 12.8 % | 21.7 % |
| Body and face (SFace, 0.55 x 1) | 44.6 % | 0.1 % | 1.9 % |
| Body and face (AuraFace, 0.50 x 1) | 48.1 % | 0.1 % | 1.9 % |
| 1920 wide: body alone / SFace 0.55 x 0.5 | 33.0 % / 57.5 % | 10.0 % / 0.2 % | 19.7 % / 0.9 % |

**By face size** (SFace at 0.50, faces clear but for their size, 1280 wide): eyes 12 to 18 px apart recognised 28 %
with 2.3 % of strangers taken; 18 to 24 px, 41 % and 1.8 %; 24 to 32 px, 55 % and 3.2 %; 48 px or more, 58 % and 1.6 %.
Under 12 px, 5 %. The gate is at 18 px.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Measured on a synthetic set (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17)
sections.text:
**Dressed alike:** with the body alone at 0.75, 32 % of the looks of strangers dressed in black were taken for a
performer (16.5 % of those in their own costume). With the safest setting, 0.0 % and 0.4 %.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Measured on a synthetic set (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17)
sections.text:
What this means:
- **The body alone at 0.75 is not safe** on this set: one stranger's look in five is taken for a performer, and one
  in three for a band dressed alike. The figures are crude, and the matcher partly matches the camera's background and
  light (each person was enrolled from every camera, which helps it most). This is the clearest reason to do the
  rehearsal before turning recognition on for stars and follow rules.
- **A clear face is far more reliable than a costume:** where a face is clear it halves the misses and all but stops
  wrong performers and strangers (0.1 %, 1.9 %), at no cost where no face is clear.
- **Faces help only where they are large enough.** At the follow loop's 640 wide, a face is usable in 6 % of looks
  (tight shots); at 1280, 17 %; at 1920, 34 %. `director_zoom_frame_width: 1280` lets faces count during the show
  (the decoder then works harder; not measured live). Face blur already looks at 1280 wide, and the People page's
  pictures are full size, so enrolment always sees the face at its best.
- **Carrying identity** adds 1 to 2.5 points at the safe setting. At body 0.75 it adds about 2 points but carries
  wrong answers too (strangers taken 16.9 % to 19.6 %): it is only as good as the matches it carries.
- Describing a person took 80 to 120 ms in the measurements (DINOv2, YuNet on the whole picture and the face model,
  with four measurements running at once); the face model alone takes 16.7 ms a face (SFace) or 138 ms (AuraFace),
  median, on the processor. At ten looks a second AuraFace is too slow for more than one face a look.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Measured on a synthetic set (M5 Pro, 2026-10-17)
sections.text:
Settings (all optional):
- `people_face_model`: `sface` (default), `auraface` or `off`.
- `people_face_model_file`: default `<data>/people/<the model's file>`.
- `people_face_threshold`, `people_face_weight`: SFace 0.55 and 1.0, AuraFace 0.50 and 1.0 (`performers.FACE_THRESHOLD`,
  `FACE_WEIGHT`).
- `people_carry_identity`: true. `people_carry_seconds`: 3.0.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Enrolling well (People page)
sections.text:
The page asks for at least three pictures of each performer: from each camera that will see them, from the front and
the side, and one close enough that their face is clear. Under each picture it shows the camera and whether the face
was found, how far apart the eyes were, and why it cannot be used (too small, turned away, looking up or down,
blurred). Under each performer it warns when there are fewer than three pictures, when they are all from one camera,
when no picture shows the face clearly (for performers whose release covers it), and when two pictures are nearly the
same (appearance similarity above 0.97).

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Reproducing
sections.text:
```
python tools/recognition_eval.py synth PORTRAITS BACKGROUNDS SYNTH --yunet face_detection_yunet_2023mar.onnx --face-model face_recognition_sface_2021dec.onnx
python tools/recognition_eval.py measure SYNTH/labels.json SAMPLES.json --appearance dinov2_small.onnx --yunet ... --face-model ... [--kind auraface] [--width 1920]
python tools/recognition_eval.py report SAMPLES.json
```
PORTRAITS is a folder per person of their photographs; BACKGROUNDS, camera frames named by camera number (01, 02,
04, 05, 06, 07). The portraits and the set itself are not in the repository.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Before going live: the rehearsal measurement
sections.text:
1. Get Consent A (with its face tick) and Consent B from 4 to 6 people (band and crew) for a 10-minute rehearsal in
   their stage clothes, on every camera, facing the cameras and turning away now and then, crossing each other.
2. Label the rehearsal's camera files: for each person, the time ranges they are in sight on each camera and where
   they are at the start of each (`LABELS.json`, identity codes only, never names; the format is at the top of
   `tools/recognition_eval.py`).
3. Run `tools/recognition_eval.py measure LABELS.json SAMPLES.json --detector yolox_s.onnx ...` (the person detector
   finds the boxes) at the width recognition will see (640 for the follow loop, 1280 for face blur), then
   `report SAMPLES.json`. It enrols half the people from one look per camera and treats the rest as strangers, 20 times
   over, and reports, for the body alone, the face alone and both, how many looks were recognised, how many were taken
   for the wrong performer and how many strangers were taken for a performer.
4. Set `people_match_threshold`, `people_face_threshold` and `people_face_weight` where no stranger is taken for a
   performer, then decide whether recognition is good enough for stars and follow rules.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Phase 2 tests (to add with the wiring)
sections.text:
- No names in `.cameras.json`, `.cuts.json`, `.looks/`, EDLs, the director's recording log, the audit log, location
  and fleet exports or update bundles, with a performer enrolled and recognised during a recorded show.
- The operator role and Stage Shots get 403 on every `/api/people/*` route, and their pages show only the ON
  indicator.
- The ON indicator appears on every page while recognition is active and on no page otherwise.
- Unknown people are never chosen as a zoom target (unless the camera's focus is the crowd), and nothing about
  them is in memory after the look.
- The VLM's prompts never contain a performer's name.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Phase 2, step 1: the fast zoom (detector only, no identity)
sections.text:
Built: `camera_manager/live.py` (a decoder kept running per followed camera) and the director's fast follow loop.
Nobody is identified. The detector finds people, and the zoom keeps to one person by position.

**Persistent decoder.** One ffmpeg per followed camera (at most 2: on air and about to be), fed the relay's spool as it
is written. It starts 1.2 s back so it has a keyframe, follows the files of a run, restarts on a new run, and keeps only
the newest picture (640 px, 10 a second, with its timing strip read). On the 4K S23 stream replayed into a spool at its
own pace:

| | Pictures/s | Bytes on disk to picture in hand (median, p95) | ffmpeg processor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Processor decode | 9.9 | 0.14 s, 0.16 s | ~30 % of one core |
| VideoToolbox | 9.9 | 0.14 s, 0.16 s | ~30 % |
| Two cameras at once (processor) | 9.7 and 9.8 | 0.14 s each | ~27 % each |
| Without `-thread_type slice` | 9.9 | **0.63 s** (frame threading holds back a picture per thread) | ~31 % |

Two ffmpeg options had to go: `-fflags nobuffer` threw away the probed keyframe, and ffmpeg's default 5 MB probe held
everything back on a low-bitrate stream. Before this, each relay picture cost about 0.4 s of processor.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Phase 2, step 1: the fast zoom (detector only, no identity)
sections.text:
**Director.** `follow_loop` runs beside the tick: every `director_zoom_detector_every_seconds` (0.1 s) it takes the
followed camera's newest picture, runs the detector, keeps plausible boxes, picks one and reframes. `pick` stays with
whoever the zoom is on, by overlap or a move of less than their own width. It lets go after
`director_zoom_follow_seconds` (1 s) unseen, and otherwise takes the tallest person.
- On a camera given a performer ("drums"), the model is still asked, at its own pace, *whom* to follow. Its answer is
  matched to the detector's look at that moment and carried forward by position (`anchor`). Until it answers, the zoom
  waits.
- Hands and two-performer shots stay with the model alone.
- With no detector model installed, everything works as before.
- The recording's log gets two fast looks a second, positions only.

End to end on the replayed walk-by (real decoder, real detector, the director against a stand-in OBS):
- A look every 0.102 s.
- While the walker was in the picture (11 s, including entering at the bottom edge), someone was followed in 93 of
  108 looks and the shot was zoomed in 89.
- In the 16 s before, nobody was followed in 155 looks.
- Before, the model's locate answered 4 to 6 s after the moment it described (live, 2026-10-16).

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Phase 2, step 1: the fast zoom (detector only, no identity)
sections.text:
Settings (all optional):
- `people_detector_model`: default `<data>/models/yolox_s.onnx`. Without it there is no fast zoom.
- `people_detector_threshold`: 0.5.
- `director_zoom_detector`: true.
- `director_zoom_detector_every_seconds`: 0.1.
- `director_zoom_follow_seconds`: 1.0.
- `director_follow_live`: true.
- `director_follow_rate`: 10.
- `director_follow_most`: 12. The most decoders kept running at once, one for each camera followed at each width
  asked for (the fast looks, each gimbal camera, the wide camera the gimbals are aimed from). Each stops by itself ten
  seconds after it was last asked for a picture.
- `director_follow_hwaccel`: `videotoolbox` on a Mac, none elsewhere. It falls back to the processor by itself.

The director's report has `follow`: how often, picture age, detector time, found.

Not yet checked on the live system with phones. To install: `pip install -r requirements-people.txt`, put
`yolox_s.onnx` (YOLOX 0.1.1rc0 release, Apache-2.0) in `<data>/models/`, and restart the manager.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Phase 2, step 2: the People page and recognition (Plus AI)
sections.text:
**Setting up:**
1. Director page → AI assistance → **Plus**.
2. The set-up lists:
   - the person detector (YOLOX-s, 35 MB)
   - the appearance model (DINOv2 small, 90 MB)
   - **Enrol the performers on the People page**, with a button to open it.

   Both downloads are checked against a pinned SHA-256 and are used as soon as they finish, with no restart.

**The People page** is under Set up, for the administrator only. *Take a picture* from a camera (the relay's
newest picture, or else OBS's). The people the detector finds are outlined: click one, or drag a box. Then add a
name, the role (Performer, or Star: priority on any camera) and instruments. Consent is one tick, or nothing under
a contract arrangement. **Add**. Under each performer:
- more pictures (*Add as: another picture of …*), and removing one
- role
- *Cameras that follow them*
- consent status, the improvement tick or its withdrawal
- **Remove and delete their data**

*Consent and keeping data* holds the contract arrangement, how long data is kept, and **Delete all performer
data**. The picture taken is held in memory for 10 minutes and served only to the administrator. Only a 160 px
thumbnail and the descriptor are kept. Each camera's *What it shows* links to the page.

**Recognition on** (*Turn on for today's show* or *at this location*): every page shows **Performer recognition:
ON** beside the show's status, for every role, and Stage Shots says so too.

sections.doc: People library: fast person detection, star performers and follow rules (design, phase 1 measurements)
sections.title: Phase 2, step 2: the People page and recognition (Plus AI)
sections.text:
**The director while it is on:**
- In each fast look, it frames a performer this camera follows first, then a star, and keeps to that person by
  position when they turn away.
- Someone not recognised as an enrolled performer is never zoomed in on. *Enrol everyone you want framed.*
- Stars are looked for in the pictures the model rates, at the same time as it rates them. A camera showing a star
  is rated `director_star_bonus` (1.5) higher when its picture is already worth showing (5 or more).
- The recording's log says "performer 2", never a name.

**Settings:**
- `people_match_threshold`: 0.75
- `people_match_margin`: 0.05
- `director_star_bonus`: 1.5
- `director_star_needs_rating`: 5
- `people_appearance_model`: default `<data>/people/dinov2_small.onnx`

**Not yet measured:** recognition accuracy with real performers. Do the rehearsal measurement above before relying
on stars and follow rules. If recognition misses, the zoom shows the whole picture rather than someone else.

- `camera_manager/performers.py`: the library (consent per purpose, encryption, retention, withdrawal, delete all,
